title: Why walking needs the ground to push you forward
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What pushes you forward when you walk?
Why can't you walk on ice?

forces.label: Ground pushes forward
forces.ask: How does the ground push me forward?

explain.say: To walk forwards you push your foot backwards against the ground. You might think you move yourself, but really it is the ground doing the pushing.

draw.text: Why walking needs the ground to push you forward

forces.label: Ground pushes forward
forces.ask: How does the ground push me forward?

explain.say: For every push there is an equal push back the other way. Your foot pushes the ground backwards, so the ground pushes your foot forwards, and that moves you along.

forces.label: Ground pushes forward
forces.ask: How does the ground push me forward?

explain.say: The ground also pushes up on you as hard as your weight pulls down, so you don't sink. And the forward push only works if friction stops your foot sliding back.

forces.label: Ground pushes forward
forces.ask: How does the ground push me forward?

explain.say: On slippery ice your foot slides backwards instead, so the ground can't push you forwards. Animals use the same trick: a horse pushes the ground back, a fish pushes water back, and a bird pushes air back.

forces.label: Ground pushes forward
forces.ask: How does the ground push me forward?

faq.q: How does the ground push me forward?
faq.a: When you walk, your foot pushes backwards on the ground. By Newton's third law, the ground pushes your foot forwards with an equal force, and friction stops your foot sliding.
asks: What pushes you when you walk?

faq.a: It says that whenever one object pushes on another, the second pushes back on the first with an equal force in the opposite direction. Forces always come in pairs.

faq.q: Why can't you walk on ice?
faq.a: Ice has very little friction, so when your foot pushes backwards it simply slides. Without grip, the ground can't push you forwards, and you slip.
asks: Why do I slip when walking on ice?

faq.q: How do fish and birds push themselves along?
faq.a: The same way. A fish pushes water backwards with its tail and the water pushes it forwards; a bird's wings push air backwards and down, and the air pushes the bird forwards and up.
asks: How does a fish swim forward?

faq.q: Does the Earth move when I walk?
faq.a: Yes, a tiny bit! You push the Earth backwards as it pushes you forwards, but the Earth is so enormous that its movement is far too small ever to notice.
asks: Do I push the Earth when I walk?

facts: Newton's third law of motion says forces always come in equal and opposite pairs.
Isaac Newton published his three laws of motion in 1687.

quiz.say: You push your foot backwards against the ground. What actually moves you forwards?
quiz.show: When you walk, what pushes you forwards?

options.show: The ground pushing your foot forwards
options.say: The ground pushing your foot forwards

quiz.why: Your foot pushes the ground backwards, and by Newton's third law the ground pushes you forwards with an equal force.

wrong.0: Weight pulls you down, not forwards.
wrong.2: Air doesn't push you along; you can walk forwards just as well into still air.
